title: A few useful IntelliJ shortcuts
answer: A few IntelliJ shortcuts I use on the default Windows/Linux keymap are: double Shift for Search Everywhere, Ctrl+Shift+N for Go to File, Ctrl+E for Recent Files, Ctrl+B for Go to Declaration, Alt+F7 for Find Usages, Ctrl+F12 for File Structure, Ctrl+Q for Quick Documentation, and Alt+Enter for intention actions and quick fixes. These shortcuts reduce mouse-driven navigation and help me move between files, symbols, usages, documentation, and fixes quickly. Shortcut keys can differ by operating system or custom keymap, so I verify the active IntelliJ keymap when working on a different setup.

steps.title: Use Search Everywhere — double Shift
steps.question: Search Everywhere reduces the need to navigate menus or project-tree folders first; you can start from what you remember about the target. IntelliJ can search classes, files, symbols, settings, and actions from one entry point. Why is double Shift a useful first shortcut to remember when you do not know exactly where something lives?
steps.why: Search Everywhere reduces the need to navigate menus or project-tree folders first; you can start from what you remember about the target.
steps.why_te: Ee IntelliJ action target code ni fast ga reach cheyyadaniki help chestundi. Search Everywhere target ekkada undo exact ga teliyakapoina class, file, symbol, setting leda action peru nundi direct ga search start cheyyadaniki help chestundi.

steps.title: Use Go to File — Ctrl+Shift+N
steps.question: Go to File searches by filename and lets you jump directly to the target without manually traversing the package tree. When you know a filename but not its folder path, why is Ctrl+Shift+N faster than expanding several project-tree directories?
steps.why: Go to File searches by filename and lets you jump directly to the target without manually traversing the package tree.
steps.why_te: Ee IntelliJ action target code ni fast ga reach cheyyadaniki help chestundi. Filename teliste Ctrl+Shift+N tho folder tree manually expand cheyyakunda direct ga target file ki vellachu.

steps.title: Use Recent Files — Ctrl+E
steps.question: Recent Files exposes the files you were just using, which is faster than searching for the same files again. Developers often switch repeatedly among a small working set of files. Why does Ctrl+E become useful during that kind of back-and-forth work?
steps.why: Recent Files exposes the files you were just using, which is faster than searching for the same files again.
steps.why_te: Ee IntelliJ action target code ni fast ga reach cheyyadaniki help chestundi. Recent Files recent ga use chesina files ni immediate ga chupistundi. Same files ni malli project tree lo search cheyyalsina avasaram taggutundi.

steps.title: Use Go to Declaration — Ctrl+B
steps.question: Go to Declaration turns a symbol reference into direct source navigation, which is especially valuable in typed Java code. Reading Java code often requires jumping from a method call or type reference to where it is declared. Why is Ctrl+B a core navigation shortcut?
steps.why: Go to Declaration turns a symbol reference into direct source navigation, which is especially valuable in typed Java code.
steps.why_te: Ee IntelliJ action target code ni fast ga reach cheyyadaniki help chestundi. Ctrl+B symbol reference nundi declaration ki direct ga teesukeltundi. Typed Java code lo implementation context fast ga understand cheyyadaniki idi useful.

steps.title: Use Find Usages — Alt+F7
steps.question: Find Usages helps estimate the impact of a change and is safer than assuming a symbol is referenced only in the file currently open. Before changing a class or method, why should you be able to see where it is used across the project?
steps.why: Find Usages helps estimate the impact of a change and is safer than assuming a symbol is referenced only in the file currently open.
steps.why_te: Ee IntelliJ action target code ni fast ga reach cheyyadaniki help chestundi. Class leda method marchadaniki mundu usages chusthe change impact entha undo telustundi. Current file matrame chusi assumption cheyyadam kanna idi safer.

steps.title: Use File Structure — Ctrl+F12
steps.question: File Structure lists the symbols inside the current file and lets you jump to the member you need. A long Java class can contain many methods and fields. Why is Ctrl+F12 useful when you want to move inside one file without scrolling through every line?
steps.why: File Structure lists the symbols inside the current file and lets you jump to the member you need.
steps.why_te: Ee IntelliJ action target code ni fast ga reach cheyyadaniki help chestundi. Ctrl+F12 current file lo methods, fields mariyu symbols list chupistundi. Long file ni full ga scroll cheyyakunda required member ki jump cheyyachu.

steps.title: Use Quick Documentation — Ctrl+Q
steps.question: Quick Documentation keeps API context beside the code and can answer many small questions without breaking the current navigation flow. When you recognize a Java or framework symbol but need its API details, why is Ctrl+Q useful before leaving the editor for external documentation?
steps.why: Quick Documentation keeps API context beside the code and can answer many small questions without breaking the current navigation flow.
steps.why_te: IntelliJ current code context batti useful information chupistundi. Ctrl+Q API documentation ni editor pakkane chupistundi. Chinna API doubts kosam external browser ki switch avvalsina avasaram taggutundi.

steps.title: Use intention actions — Alt+Enter
steps.question: Intention actions surface relevant fixes or improvements exactly where the IDE detects a problem or opportunity. IntelliJ can suggest imports, fixes, and context-aware transformations at the caret. Why is Alt+Enter one of the most useful shortcuts to know? The Use intention actions — Alt+Enter action exposes the relevant IntelliJ state directly, so the question stays tied to observable project behavior rather than generic interview wording.
steps.why: Intention actions surface relevant fixes or improvements exactly where the IDE detects a problem or opportunity.
steps.why_te: IntelliJ current code context batti useful information chupistundi. Alt+Enter current caret context ki relevant fixes, imports leda improvements ni direct ga chupistundi. Problem unna place nundi action start cheyyachu.
